svg.data-what: the digestive tract seen from the front, from the oesophagus to the rectum, with the liver, gallbladder and pancreas: the right side of the body is on the left of the picture

path.data-what: the oesophagus, the muscular tube that carries swallowed food from the throat to the stomach

g.data-what: the small intestine, about six metres coiled in the middle of the abdomen: jejunum then ileum, where food is absorbed
the stomach: it churns food with acid and enzymes before passing it on through the pylorus

path.data-what: the common bile duct, carrying bile from the liver and gallbladder into the duodenum

g.data-what: the pancreas, its head in the curve of the duodenum: digestive juices into the gut, insulin and glucagon into the blood

path.data-what: the duodenum, the first C-shaped part of the small intestine, where bile and pancreatic juice arrive

g.data-what: the ascending colon, climbing the right side of the abdomen; the large intestine absorbs water and holds the bacteria of the gut
the transverse colon, hanging across the abdomen; the large intestine absorbs water and holds the bacteria of the gut
the descending colon, down the left side; the large intestine absorbs water and holds the bacteria of the gut
the sigmoid colon, the S-shaped bend into the rectum; the large intestine absorbs water and holds the bacteria of the gut

path.data-what: the appendix, a narrow blind tube hanging from the caecum
the caecum, the pouch where the small intestine opens into the large intestine
the rectum and anal canal, the end of the tract

g.data-what: the liver, the largest organ inside the body: it makes bile, stores sugar, and cleans the blood coming from the gut

path.data-what: the gallbladder, under the liver, storing bile between meals
